subject: Streaming SLA: token emission & sustained-rate exception request
messages:
From: Julie Nguyen <julie.nguyen@fastretail.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T18:12:00Z
Subject: Streaming endpoint behavior in our edge regions — possible SLA carve-out?

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from our engineering team after the last integration test: in our APAC edge pop (we're caching regional content), the streaming endpoints are regularly seeing an extra 6–12s time-to-first-token compared to US tests and sustained token emission sometimes drops under the expected 400 tokens/sec when responses exceed 5k tokens. This is causing a poor UX in our in-store kiosks (slow first-char feedback).

Do you have a formal process for requesting a temporary SLA exception (we'd propose a streaming TTFT target of 15s and a sustained baseline of 300 tokens/sec for the APAC-pop traffic for a 90-day remediation window)? If you need traces I can attach a short capture.

Thanks,
Julie Nguyen
Senior Product Manager — FastRetail
julie.nguyen@fastretail.com

Attachment: network-trace-2027-03-28.txt (text)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Julie Nguyen <julie.nguyen@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Streaming endpoint behavior in our edge regions — possible SLA carve-out?

Julie — thanks for the trace, I pulled it into the ticket. I'm looping in Marcus (SRE/Platform) and Lauren (AM lead) to scope a formal exception. High level: we do have a documented carve-out process for streaming where network or customer-edge latency causes elevated TTFT or lower sustained token emission. We typically require:

- concrete trace artifacts and a short business impact statement (you provided both)
- a remediation plan (networking, routing, or model warm-up changes) and owner
- an agreed monitoring window with target metrics and rollback criteria

Marcus — can you review Julie's snippet and propose the monitoring window and a measurement method (p99 TTFT and 1-minute rolling tokens/sec) we can commit to in an amendment?

Julie — attaching the trace you sent to our ticket; we will aim to have a draft amendment by end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0172
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T21:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Streaming endpoint behavior in our edge regions — possible SLA carve-out?

Team — I looked through the trace. Observations:

- The TTFT spikes correlate with cross-region routing into the US serving pool (adds ~80–120ms per hop during peak) plus a cold-LRU miss on the prefix cache for long generations.
- Sustained emission drops are happening when model context length > 4k tokens; batching/backpressure causes token/sec variability for small windows.

Proposal for amendment metrics:

1) Time-to-first-token (p99) for streaming endpoints: default hosted SLA 4s in-region; carve-out for the affected APAC pop to p99 <= 15s for a 90-day period. Measurement: synthetic probes from the FastRetail pop + sampled production traces (1% sampling).
2) Sustained emission: rolling 60s tokens/sec measured p50/p95. For the carve-out, baseline of 300 tokens/sec p50 and 200 tokens/sec p95 for responses >2,000 tokens.
3) Rollback criteria: if errors >0.5% or customer observes correctness regressions, immediate review and potential suspension of the carve-out.

I'll prepare a short CSV with the probes and a sketch of the wording. Also recommend we include an autoscaling/capacity note — if FastRetail wants hard throughput guarantees we'll need reserved capacity; otherwise this is a temporary operational exception.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:17:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Streaming endpoint behavior in our edge regions — possible SLA carve-out?

Forwarding to get sign-off language. I agree with Marcus's measurement approach; two additional asks before we send to FastRetail legal:

- Add a monitoring dashboard link and who on our side owns on-call during the 90-day window.
- Limit the carve-out to the specific endpoint(s) and model variants (e.g., text-gen-v3-stream) — no blanket streaming SLA change.

I'll approve the amendment draft provided the DocuSign amendment includes a fixed end date (90 days) and an option to extend by mutual written consent. Marcus — can you add the SRE on-call escalation contact and an example dashboard URL?

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Julie Nguyen <julie.nguyen@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, legal@fastretail.com
Date: 2027-04-02T14:09:00Z
Subject: Approved: temporary streaming SLA amendment (APAC pop) — next steps

Julie — good news. We've reviewed the trace, scoped metrics, and Lauren has approved a 90-day temporary amendment limited to the affected APAC edge pop and the text-gen-v3-stream model variant. Summary of the agreed points: 

- Effective carve-out window: 2027-04-05 through 2027-07-04 (90 days).
- p99 TTFT target for the affected pop: <= 15s (measured by synthetic probes + 1% sampled traces).
- Sustained emission baseline: 300 tokens/sec p50; 200 tokens/sec p95 for responses >2,000 tokens.
- Rollback/exit triggers: errors >0.5% or correctness regressions.
- Ownership: Redwood SRE on-call (pager: +1 415 555 0100) and Redwood platform dashboard (https://internal.redwood.ai/dash/FR-2027-09-EXP) will be shared with FastRetail read-only.
- Note: If FastRetail wants hard throughput guarantees beyond this temporary carve-out we will need a Dedicated capacity commit; Marcus: please add that note to the amendment.

Attached: SLA-amendment-draft.pdf (draft amendment with measurement clauses). For signatures, we plan to use DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/some-doc-id

Can you confirm FastRetail legal (cc'd) is OK with the 90-day window and monitoring approach? Once legal confirms, I'll push the amendment to DocuSign and get countersigned.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Attachment: SLA-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF)
